A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DOVE study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, proofs, and appendices are readable and can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original comparisons across 12 LLMs, validity and reliability experiments, ablations, and human evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds MAUVE comparisons, a codebook-consolidation ablation, and human and model-based validation of value priming.

M1.justification: The rate-distortion optimizer, value recognition procedure, and UOT/Sinkhorn scoring remain unchanged. Appendix F.2 newly describes disambiguating duplicate code names, without establishing a substantive algorithm change. The revised reconstruction sample count is an experimental setting.

E1.justification: Both versions use 824 topics, 15,213 human-written documents, the same four cultures, and the same downstream datasets: KOLD, JOLFCC, COLD, HateXplain, and D3CODE. Additional analyses examine existing representations and priming tasks; the DeepSeek replication changes the model configuration.

E2.justification: Two focused comparators are added: MAUVE under three representations (v3 Table 3) and GPT-5.2-based codebook consolidation (Table 11). WVS, GOQA, CDEval, NormAd, NaVAB, and the existing ablation comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported reconstruction sampling parameter N2 from 3 to 1, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added protocols evaluate three MAUVE representations, repeat priming with DeepSeek V3.2, and have two South Korean annotators judge 50 primed/control document pairs.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends checks of the central components and validation assumptions: MAUVE comparisons separate representation and metric effects, prompt-based consolidation tests optimization beyond semantic grouping, and human judgments plus a second priming backbone test whether the manipulation works. Existing ablations, sensitivity analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Existing human evaluations replace pairwise Cohen's kappa reporting with Fleiss' kappa. The new priming study also reports agreement, at 0.814. The three-split/three-trial reliability design and Cronbach's alpha/CV reporting remain unchanged; additional repetitions of retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the matched appendix score tables retain their values. Added results include MAUVE correlations of -5.73%, 23.04%, and 29.78% for document, expression, and code representations; 24.51% for prompt-based consolidation; DeepSeek V3.2 priming shifts of 11.72%, 2.03%, and -2.37%; and a reported 95% human priming win rate. Agreement values change under the replacement statistic, including mean kappa from 0.661 to 0.644.

T1.justification: The variational derivations, entropy-approximation proposition and proof, and UOT/Sinkhorn mathematics are retained. Additional empirical scoring formulas, displayed equations, and notation corrections do not introduce new theoretical results or substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects the stated corpus contribution from 14K to 15K documents, consistent with the 15,213 already reported in both versions. The C3 framing, methodological contribution, 31.56% predictive correlation, and reliability claim with 500 samples remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new comparisons as support for value representations, UOT, and iterative optimization. Appendix D.4 addresses possible priming failure, while G.1 argues that DOVE requires no more prior cultural knowledge than the baselines. The internet-sampling, four-country, and subcultural limitations already appear in v1 and are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly specifies GOQA's similarity calculation and CDEval's normalization, consistency weighting, and profile comparison. Appendix F.2 adds code-name finalization details. These expand documentation of existing procedures; prompts, corpus construction details, cost estimates, and repository access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is condensed, removing citations including Ren et al. (2024), Ji et al. (2025), and Scherrer et al. (2023). Lin et al. (2024) is added to support ICL steering. Choi et al. (2025) and Song et al. (2026) share the cited arXiv identifier and represent an updated reference.

P1.justification: v3 makes local language corrections, changes 'polishment' to 'refinement,' condenses related work, and adds acknowledgments and conference front matter. Topic composition moves from Appendix C into Section 4.4, and the opening appendices are reordered. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the overall pipeline diagram, three comparison tables, and a priming chart, and redraws the construction, recognition, and refinement diagrams. The topic map moves into the main text, existing human-evaluation results are redisplayed there, and appendix table rows and columns are reordered. Figure 14 incorrectly repeats the extraction chart under a topic-quality caption.

improvement.justification: The new MAUVE and consolidation controls and direct priming checks strengthen validation, while fuller baseline scoring details improve reproducibility. These targeted gains improve an otherwise retained study. They outweigh the localized Figure 14 error, whose plot conflicts with its caption and the unchanged topic-quality results in the accompanying text.
